summary.title: Raft Consensus Algorithm
summary.one_liner: Raft is a consensus algorithm designed to be easier to understand than Paxos while matching its fault tolerance and performance, and this page links to the paper, visualizations, talks, university courses, and implementations.
keywords: in search of an understandable consensus algorithm
takeaways: Raft is a consensus algorithm claimed to be equivalent to Paxos in fault tolerance and performance but easier to understand, being decomposed into relatively independent subproblems.
Consensus systems keep making progress while a majority of servers is available; a 5-server cluster tolerates 2 failures.
Consensus is used to agree on commands in replicated state machines so every server applies the same command sequence.
The page points to the original Raft paper, Ongaro's dissertation (with membership change and TLA+ spec), RaftScope, and a list of talks.
It also lists university courses with Raft lectures or assignments and a table of community implementations.
summary.summary: This is a resource hub for the Raft consensus algorithm. It explains the core idea: consensus among servers that makes progress when a majority is available, applied through replicated state machines and logs. It then links to the Raft paper by Ongaro and Ousterhout, Ongaro's PhD dissertation, an interactive browser visualization (RaftScope), and a long list of talks and papers. It ends with courses that teach Raft and a comparison table of open-source implementations.
